scope: Six fixed synthetic English diagnostics; not a teaching-quality benchmark

cases.scenario: Synthetic cafe check: order one apple. Each character replies with one short sentence.
cases.ground_truth: An apple and one apple are both valid. You are welcome and You're welcome are both valid. Do not invent mandatory article or contraction rules.
Both are standard English. An is appropriate before apple's vowel sound; a contraction is optional.

cases.scenario: Compare these examples as standard written English.
cases.ground_truth: Saw is correct here in standard written English. Bare seen needs correction; I have seen her yesterday is not the straightforward correction. Do not make universal claims about dialects.

utterances: My friend Alex said they are ready.
cases.ground_truth: Singular they is valid; they are agrees; gender is unspecified; present are may describe continuing readiness. Do not force he/she, they is, or mandatory backshift.

cases.scenario: Compare these phrases without assuming whether the speaker means meat or a whole bird.
cases.ground_truth: Both may be grammatical. Chicken may mean meat; a chicken may mean one whole bird, including a cooked one. Explain context or uncertainty; do not confidently correct either.

cases.scenario: Compare these phrases without assuming attendance versus a particular destination.
cases.ground_truth: Both may be grammatical. Attendance and a particular school/destination differ by context. Do not universally forbid or require the article.
